verses.133:1a: {ecce}, bendizei {dominum}, * todos os servos do Senhor:
verses.133:1b: {quistatis} na casa do Senhor, * nos átrios da casa do nosso Deus.
verses.133:2: Nas noites {extollite} as vossas mãos {insancta}, * e bendizei {dominum}.

decisions.why: ecce + imperative is a Hebraism through the Greek (ἰδοὺ δή). Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT drop ecce and turn nunc into a connective ('Agora, pois'); DRB keeps both words ('Behold now bless ye'). At Compline the nunc is heard as the hour itself, beside 'In nóctibus'.

options.label: Eis agora
options.note: Draft. Both Latin words, in the Latin's order; 'eis' is the standing Portuguese for ecce and needs no footnote.

options.label: Agora, pois
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT. Smooth, but ecce goes unheard and 'pois' makes an inference the Latin does not make.

options.label: Vede, agora
options.note: Turns the particle into a verb, as 'Behold' does; it then piles two imperatives ('Vede… bendizei') where the Latin has one.

decisions.why: The psalter has benedícere with the accusative (here, 15:7, 33:2) and with the dative (102:20–22 Benedícite Dómino, 134:19–20, 67:27, 113:26 — checked in the DO Latin). Portuguese can keep the difference for nothing: direct object for the accusative, 'ao Senhor' for the dative.

options.label: o Senhor
options.note: Draft, with pt-PT. The accusative as a direct object; leaves 'ao Senhor' for the psalms that have Dómino.

options.label: ao Senhor
options.note: Matos Soares 1932, and the Diurnal Monástico 1962 ('bendizei ao Senhor'): the devotional habit of the preposition before God's name. Good Portuguese; it only gives up the Latin's two constructions.

decisions.why: stare is to stand, and the Greek is ἑστῶτες, 'standing' (DRB 'Who stand'): the servants are on their feet, ministering, at night. pt-PT flattens it to 'estais'; Matos Soares has the old 'assistis'. The verse also opens on a relative that hangs from the vocative of 133:1a, and the two halves of a choir say them in turn.

options.label: Que estais de pé
options.note: Draft. The concrete posture kept (rule 5). Opening the verse on 'Que', dependent on the verse before, is what the Latin does (Qui statis) and what Dom Marcos does in the Diurnal ('Que permaneceis na casa do Senhor').

options.label: Vós que estais de pé
options.note: Names the subject (allowed by rule 2) so that the verse can stand alone when the other side of the choir takes it; one syllable more (+3 on the Latin by checks.py).

options.label: Vós que estais
options.note: pt-PT. The smoothest, and 'estar' is stare's own child; but the standing is lost.

decisions.why: The psalter lifts hands, eyes and souls with several verbs — leváre (120:1, 122:1), extóllere (here; 27:2 dum extóllo manus meas; 74:6), eleváre (140:2), exaltáre — and they should not all become one Portuguese verb. extóllere is 'to lift out or up, to raise up' (L&S).

options.label: erguei
options.note: Draft, from the Diurnal Monástico 1962 ('Erguei vossas mãos'). Leaves 'levantar' free for leváre and 'elevar' for eleváre. The vós imperative is safe: 'erguei' is not 'ergui'.

options.label: levantai
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT. Just as plain; but it is the natural word for leváre ('Levávi óculos meos'), and it is one vowel from the past 'levantei'.

options.label: elevai
options.note: A little more solemn; it is the cognate of another verb of the psalter, eleváre (140:2 elevátio mánuum meárum).

decisions.why: A neuter plural adjective used as a noun, after the Greek εἰς τὰ ἅγια: 'toward the holy (places)', that is, the sanctuary. DRB 'to the holy places'; Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT 'para o santuário'. The psalter also has the noun sanctuárium (72:17, 73:7, 82:13, 88:40) and the singular 'in sancto' (21:4, 59:8, 62:3, 76:14, 150:1 in sanctis), so the choice here touches those places.

options.label: para o lugar santo
options.note: Draft. Keeps sanctus audible and keeps sancta apart from sanctuárium → santuário. The Greek plural names one place, so the singular.

options.label: para o santuário
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT (the Diurnal too: 'na direção do santuário'). What the phrase means, in one word; it merges sancta with sanctuárium.

options.label: para os lugares santos
options.note: DRB's plural. In Brazil 'os lugares santos' are the pilgrimage sites of the Holy Land.

decisions.why: The whole psalm turns on one verb said three times: benedícite… benedícite… Benedícat — bless the Lord, and the Lord bless you. Portuguese has two verbs, bendizer (to speak well of, to bless God) and abençoar (to give a blessing), and every parallel splits them here (MS1932, pt-PT, Diurnal: 'abençoe'). Rule 2 forbids dropping a repetition the Latin has; but 'abençoar' is what any Brazilian says. benedícere with God as subject recurs (66:7–8 Benedícat nos Deus, 127:5 Benedícat tibi Dóminus ex Sion), so this wants a ruling.

options.label: te bendiga
options.note: Draft. One verb, as in the Latin: bendizei… bendizei… bendiga. 'Bendizer' with God as subject is dictionary Portuguese ('Deus te bendiga'), a little old-fashioned, understood at once.

options.label: te abençoe
options.note: Matos Soares 1932, pt-PT, Diurnal Monástico 1962. The everyday word for what God does; the psalm's hinge — the same verb going up and coming down — is no longer heard.

decisions.latin: Benedícat te Dóminus ex Sion, * qui fecit cælum et terram.
decisions.why: In natural Portuguese order the relative lands next to 'Sião' ('de Sião, que fez o céu e a terra'), and Sion would seem to have made heaven and earth. The Latin's masculine 'qui' cannot mislead. 'qui fecit cælum et terram' is a formula (113:23, 120:2, 123:8, 145:6), so the words 'que fez o céu e a terra' should stay fixed whatever is done around them.

options.label: O Senhor te bendiga de Sião, * ele que fez…

forms.v3: O Senhor {benedicat} de Sião, * ele que fez o céu e a terra.

options.note: Draft. Natural order, and the subject named again at the mediant — DRB 'he that made', and the Diurnal Monástico 1962 'Êle que fêz o céu e a terra', from which the 'ele' is taken. The formula itself is untouched.

options.label: Bendiga-te de Sião o Senhor, * que fez…

forms.v3: {benedicat_encl} de Sião o Senhor, * que fez o céu e a terra.

options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT: verb first, as in the Latin, and 'o Senhor' moved to the mediant so that the relative finds it. Nothing supplied; but it is an inversion nobody would say, in a verse said every night.

choices.133:1a: benedícite → bendizei (safe at the vós imperative: the past is 'bendisse'). 'Senhor' closes both cola, and the first colon of 133:1b too: the Latin does the same (Dóminum / Dómini / Dómini). 'omnes servi Dómini' is a vocative; no 'vós' or 'ó' is supplied (Matos Soares adds 'vós', the Diurnal 'ó'). servus → servo, as in the Nunc dimittis (servum tuum).
choices.133:1b: The verse hangs from the vocative of 133:1a, as in the Latin. 'átrios' kept (átrium; the courts of the Temple): a word still used of churches. 'domus' → casa both times. The Hebrew has no second colon here and puts 'in the nights' in this verse; the Latin follows the LXX and so does the translation.
choices.133:2: 'In nóctibus' is plural (LXX ἐν ταῖς νυξίν; DRB 'In the nights'): 'Nas noites', not pt-PT's 'De noite'. It is the word that makes this a psalm of Compline. Second colon −2 on the Latin, within range.
choices.133:3: The psalm turns from the plural servants (vós) to a singular 'te': 'te', with tu-forms nowhere else needed. 'ex Sion' → 'de Sião' (MS1932, pt-PT, Diurnal); 'desde Sião' would mark the origin more plainly but is heavier. 127:5 has the same blessing with the dative (Benedícat tibi Dóminus ex Sion) and should follow whatever is ruled here.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm133.txt. The project reports that it was collated against the printed Hetzenauer 1914 Clementine (pp. 557–558) with no divergence of wording; I did not re-read the page.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps133.md. Bolls files this psalm's Douay-Rheims as Ps 135 and parallels.py found it (the text shown is the right psalm). The Latin follows the LXX against the Hebrew in 133:1b (the second colon, 'in átriis domus Dei nostri', is not in the Hebrew) and in placing 'In nóctibus' at the head of 133:2. Occurrences quoted in the decisions (benedícere + accusative / dative, extóllere, sanctuárium / in sancto, qui fecit cælum et terram, ex Sion) were checked with grep in the DO Latin psalter, not recalled. Address: vós for the servants, tu for the 'te' of 133:3.
